claim: A real panic button + SOC trail for a local-first creature. SAFE STATE: one incident.lockdown() call forces EVERY outward capability OFF (mail/imessage/web/host_awareness/calendar/reminders/notes/grow_intelligence), enforced at the gate (caps.enabled returns False while locked) regardless of what the user had enabled. AUDITED: the lockdown is recorded (status.locked + reason) and written to an append-only, timestamped, local security event trail. REVERSIBLE: restore() lifts the lockdown and hands the user's STORED settings back intact (lockdown overrides, never deletes). IDEMPOTENT: a second lockdown is safe; restoring with nothing active is a no-op. Triggerable from the CLI (python3 -m anima.incident lockdown/restore/status) with a runbook (docs/incident_response.md) and a GRC control map (docs/compliance_controls.md).
owner: anima/incident.py (lockdown/restore/status/security_event/recent_events), anima/caps.py (enabled() honors incident.is_locked), scripts/certify_incident_response.py, docs/incident_response.md, docs/compliance_controls.md

killer_test.name: lockdown_safe_state_audited_reversible_soc_trail
killer_test.setup: scripts/certify_incident_response.py proves (hermetic): with several caps enabled, lockdown() forces every outward capability OFF at the caps gate; the lockdown is recorded + written to the security event trail; restore() lifts it and the user's stored settings read True again (override, not delete); a second lockdown is safe and restore-with-nothing is a no-op; the event trail is append-only + queryable + timestamped; and caps.enabled itself checks incident.is_locked().

known_gaps: Lockdown is manual (CLI/API) by design — no auto-trip heuristic yet (avoids false-positive self-lockouts; an Argus-signal auto-trip is tracked). A one-click dashboard button is the surfacing step; the mechanism + CLI + runbook are complete. Event sources currently include lockdown/restore + any caller of security_event; wiring more passive sources (auth failures, injection flags) is incremental.
